metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to find the 2019 NFL Super Bowl score on nfl.com but failed at 50 turns. The model reached the NFL homepage, accepted cookie consent, and clicked the GAMES menu where a dropdown with Playoffs items was visible.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome, click navigation menus on NFL website, accept cookie banners, use GAMES dropdown.
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed at step 3 when it waited instead of clicking the dropdown item. Subsequent navigation was unreliable.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to navigating to the playoffs section, which is a direct sub-goal reachable from GAMES > Playoffs. This tests the ability to use the GAMES navigation dropdown successfully.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating from the NFL homepage to the playoffs section. The evaluator checks that the active URL matches 'nfl.com.*playoff'. Initial state (nfl.com/International) does not match, providing negative-control resistance.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'active_url_from_accessTree' correctly extracts the active browser URL from Chrome's accessibility tree, which is the right state to check for a URL navigation task.
Metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' correctly handles the 'type: rule' parameter convention: it receives the rules dict directly and accesses rules['expected'] — no incorrect nesting.

Regex pattern 'nfl\.com.*playoff' semantically matches any playoffs-related URL on the NFL website (e.g. nfl.com/playoffs/, nfl.com/playoff-picture), providing correct and sufficiently broad coverage.
Initial state URL (https://www.nfl.com/) does not contain 'playoff', so negative-control resistance is present — the evaluator will not pass a do-nothing agent.
The single instruction requirement (navigate to the playoffs section of nfl.com) is fully covered by this one URL pattern check; no additional steps are missing.
